title: News Ltd. Takes a 40% Stake in the News of the World After Maxwell Bid
description_short: News Ltd. Takes a 40% Stake in the News of the World After Maxwell Bid
description_medium: The Guardian’s 1968 archive reports that Rupert Murdoch’s News Ltd. was to take a 40% stake in the News of the World after Robert Maxwell’s Pergamon Press failed in a takeover bid. Murdoch was to become joint managing director. The linked report documents this British newspaper transaction, but it does not establish any connection to Donald Trump.
description_long: A Guardian archive report dated October 25, 1968, said effective control of the News of the World was passing to the Australian newspaper company News Ltd. The report described a deal intended to defeat a takeover bid by Pergamon Press, the publishing group headed by Robert Maxwell. Under the announced arrangement, News Ltd. was to take a 40% stake in the Sunday newspaper, which the article described as Britain’s largest-circulation Sunday paper. Rupert Murdoch, News Ltd.’s chairman, was to become joint managing director alongside the paper’s existing chairman, Sir William Carr. The article documents the proposed ownership transaction and management change. It does not mention Donald Trump or establish why this historical newspaper event belongs in a Trump-related record. The event can be described from the Guardian report, but the record still needs evidence of a direct Trump connection or confirmation that it should be retained as an unrelated historical item.
notes: The Guardian archive page is accessible and is dated October 25, 1968.
